analysis.title: GS US Daily Download 1 Oct 2026
key_insights: Core PCE rose 0.25% in August, somewhat below expectations, and the year-over-year rate is 3.01%, well below expectations. The downward revision from methodological changes was larger than GS expected, mostly from the portfolio management component.

GS now expects 3.0% core PCE growth on a Q4/Q4 basis, well below the median FOMC participant forecast of 3.4%. GS thinks an October hike is unlikely and pushes the second hike in its forecast to December. It sees a strong chance the FOMC concludes additional hikes are unnecessary.

GS upgrades OXY and raises its 12-month price target to $69. Reasons: differentiated advanced recovery approach, debt reduction and dividend growth outlook, a $4.0bn cash flow improvement target by 2030, and a discounted valuation.

GS downgrades TOU to Sell with a lowered 12-month price target of C$49. Reasons: a weak near-term Western Canadian natural gas backdrop, a premium valuation relative to peers, and delays to a sustainable FCF inflection after the one-year NEBC infrastructure buildout pause.

GS expects Micron to trade modestly higher after a strong quarter and guidance well ahead of the Street, partly offset by modest gross margin downside and elevated expectations. Supply/demand stays tight in DRAM and NAND through 2027 and 2028.

Micron signed 10 additional long-term agreements, now about 35% of expected revenue through FY30. About 75% of these contain structured pricing frameworks. GS sees them as a positive that could raise the multiple investors pay on peak earnings.

GS stays Neutral on Micron. It would turn more constructive if supply growth discipline continues across the industry through 2028 and beyond. Industry supply additions are accelerating, but GS does not expect meaningful slack until 2028 at the earliest.

DoorDash announced product and platform updates at Dash Forward 2026 on September 30. GS reads them as DASH evolving from a food delivery platform toward a three-sided local commerce company, with management balancing growth investment against margins.
Month-end showed an $11.5B market-on-close sell imbalance. Pensions were modeled to sell $30.5B of US equities, in the 89th percentile over the past three years.

Activity was spotty given performance challenges, the focus on oil and rates, the midterm overhang, and fast narrative shifts in AI. Yields rose again as the Street looked through the softer PCE (+25bps vs +30bps expected).

The tape had an unwind flavor, with short interest and non-profitable tech outperforming. Software outperformed semis. JBL fell 10% on a beat/raise, weighing on sentiment into MU, while FDS rose 4% on a mixed print and outlook.

GS floor activity was a 4 on a 1-10 scale, finishing +6% net to buy. Asset managers were net buyers (tech and macro) and hedge funds were roughly flat, with demand in healthcare against supply in tech and industrials.
Chart of the day: options on FICC-based ETFs have tripled in volume over the last 2 weeks.

TOU (Tourmaline) faces a weak near-term Western Canadian gas backdrop, a premium valuation, and delayed FCF inflection after the NEBC buildout pause.
Strong quarter and guidance well ahead of the Street, but GS sees roughly balanced risk/reward. It would turn more constructive if industry supply discipline holds through 2028.

JBL fell 10% on a beat/raise, and FDS rose 4% on a mixed print and outlook (price moves as stated in the market update).
Micron's long-term agreements now cover about 35% of expected revenue through FY30, with about 75% containing structured pricing frameworks.
